strengths: Clear problem identification: The paper effectively motivates two concrete limitations of existing KD methods (softmax smoothing and DLD's solution space restriction) with compelling examples (Figure 1)

Sound theoretical contributions: Proposition 1, Theorem 2, and Theorem 3 are rigorously proven and provide theoretical guarantees. Theorem 2 particularly establishes that CSD's solution set properly contains DLD's, addressing logit shift invariance
Efficient gradient computation: Theorem 3's reduction from O(|V|²) objective to O(|V|) gradient via clever factorization w(y,x)=w₁(y)w₂(x) is non-trivial and practically valuable

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple benchmarks (5 instruction-following + 3 task-specific), model scales (0.1B-7B), 10+ baselines, multiple metrics (ROUGE-L, Self-BLEU, Distinct-N, GPT-4), and ablations strengthen claims

Design space exploration: The parameterization by (w₁, w₂) enabling mode-seeking/mode-covering variants is elegant, and Figure 3a shows CSD enveloping the diversity-fidelity frontier of existing methods
Consistent improvements: CSD shows improvements across all evaluated settings and works orthogonally with on-policy methods (Table 2), suggesting broad applicability
Practical algorithm with clear implementation: Algorithm 1 and Code 1 provide implementable solutions, addressing the training instability problem through well-motivated logarithmic transformation
weaknesses: Modest empirical improvements with fairness concerns: Average improvement 20.65 (CSD) vs 20.00 (SRKL) in Table 1 is 0.65 ROUGE-L points with overlapping error bars. Critical fairness issue: OpenLLaMA experiments fix CSD's learning rate to 1e-4 without tuning while baselines use official settings. Task-specific distillation shows validation loss unavailable for CSD, affecting checkpoint selection fairness

Incremental conceptual novelty: Core contribution adapts existing concrete score matching (Meng et al. 2022) to autoregressive LLMs. While solving practical issues, the conceptual novelty is moderate. Logarithmic transformation for training stability is straightforward

Theory-practice gap: Theorems assume 'sufficient model capacity' without quantification. No analysis of why/when the larger solution set helps under limited capacity (the practical scenario). Empirical validation (Figure 8) limited to one setting. No convergence analysis or sample complexity bounds

Unexplained baseline failures: Table 3 shows TV/SKL/SRKL achieve 0% accuracy on GSM8K versus 25.78% for CSD, but lacks mechanistic analysis. Receives only speculation about 'mode-seeking tendencies.' Case studies (Tables 7-10) are superficial

Limited ablation studies: Only T/U/S weighting choices evaluated in Table 4. Monte Carlo comparison (Figure 5) only for (S,S). No systematic sensitivity analysis across tasks. Restrictive factorization assumption w(y,x)=w₁(y)w₂(x) not justified

Limited scope and scalability: Maximum model size 7B (relatively small). No evaluation on 13B/70B models. No multilingual evaluation. No actual wall-clock time comparisons despite efficiency claims. O(|V|) gradient complexity still involves 50K+ vocabulary operations

Experimental concerns affecting confidence: OpenLLaMA results potentially biased by inconsistent hyperparameter tuning. Task-specific checkpoint selection differs between CSD and baselines. Only 5 random seeds for main results

Incomplete theoretical justification: 'Sufficient capacity' assumption undefined quantitatively. No degradation analysis when capacity insufficient. Weighting factorization lacks theoretical motivation beyond enabling efficiency

strengths: Clear problem motivation: Figure 1 effectively demonstrates how softmax smoothing and DLD's solution set restrictions limit existing approaches
Solid theoretical contributions: Proposition 1 establishes consistency, Theorem 2 rigorously shows the broader solution set of CSD, and Theorem 3 provides efficient O(|V|) gradient computation
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse settings (task-agnostic, task-specific, general chat) with multiple teacher-student pairs and 10+ baselines
Thorough ablation studies examining weighting functions, fidelity-diversity trade-offs, temperature scaling, calibration, and gradient computation methods
Practical design with clean algorithms (Algorithm 1), reference code, and demonstrated orthogonal integration with on-policy methods (Table 2)
Rich analysis with insightful visualizations (Figures 9-13) showing solution set exploration and logit offset dynamics supporting theoretical claims
weaknesses: Modest empirical improvements: Gains are often 1-2% over baselines (e.g., 20.65 vs 20.00 SRKL in Table 1; 7.42 vs 7.28 MT-Bench in Table 4) with no statistical significance testing to validate claims of consistent superiority

Experimental fairness concerns: Baselines (SKL, AB) underperform compared to original papers; CSD uses fixed learning rate (1e-4) while baselines use original settings; raises questions about equal hyperparameter tuning

Limited theoretical analysis: Theorem 2 proves Θ*_CSD ⊃ Θ*_DLD but lacks analysis of why larger solution sets improve generalization; connection between logit shift invariance and better performance is only empirically demonstrated

Arbitrary weighting function design: Default choice of 'detached student probability' lacks clear justification; limited guidance for practitioners on choosing w1, w2 for new tasks; adaptive weighting (Section D.2) appears ad-hoc

Incremental novelty: Concrete score matching is from Meng et al. (2022); main contributions are addressing instability via log transformation and efficient gradient computation—solid engineering but limited conceptual novelty

Limited experimental scope: Largest student model is 3B (from 7B teacher); no evaluation on larger students, non-standard architectures (MoE, sparse), or specialized domains; missing comparisons with recent work (e.g., speculative distillation cited but not compared)

Computational cost not clearly advantageous: Table 9 shows training time sometimes higher than baselines (26.64s vs 25.84s for KL); no discussion of scalability to massive vocabularies (256k) or per-token overhead
Incomplete failure mode analysis: Table 3 shows DLD at 0% accuracy on GSM8K with only speculative explanation about mode-seeking; deeper investigation of when/why CSD excels would strengthen claims
